full_name: Institute for AI Policy and Strategy
mission: IAPS is a nonpartisan think tank producing policy research on AI and national security, from today's frontier models to possible AGI and superintelligence. Its work covers frontier security, compute policy and export controls, and international strategy including US–China crisis communication, and it runs an AI policy fellowship.

key_work.title: Cloud Compute: A Policy Escalation Framework
key_work.plain_summary: Chinese developers can rent advanced US chips through overseas cloud providers; IAPS proposes a cloud-compute rule and step-by-step escalation options to close this gap.

key_work.title: Differential Automation: Steering Automated Research and Development Toward Safety and Security
key_work.plain_summary: As AI companies automate their own research, IAPS argues a deliberate share of that AI-driven R&D should go to safety and security work, not just capabilities.

key_work.title: Honeypots for AI Agent Insider Threats
key_work.plain_summary: Treats deployed AI agents like potential insider threats and proposes decoy 'honeypots' inside systems to catch unauthorised actions.

key_work.title: Establishing a US–China AI Risk and Incident Dialogue
key_work.plain_summary: Proposes a channel for the US and China to notify each other quickly about serious AI incidents, with a standard template.

key_work.title: Near-Term Verification Methods for AI Chip Exports
key_work.plain_summary: Looks at practical ways to check where exported AI chips end up and how they are used.

key_work.title: Embedded Evaluators for Frontier AI: Contractual Foundations for Credible Assessments
key_work.plain_summary: Sets out five contract terms needed for in-house independent evaluators at AI companies to be a real check.

warnings.text: Remote cloud access lets adversaries use the most advanced US compute despite export controls.
Fully automated AI R&D (recursive self-improvement) could compress timelines for putting safeguards in place.
AI agents deployed at scale create a new kind of insider threat.
Increasingly capable offensive cyber agents threaten under-resourced defenders such as utilities and hospitals.

recommendations.text: Issue a cloud-compute export rule with an escalation framework.
Direct a meaningful share of AI-automated R&D toward safety and security ('differential automation').
Set up a US–China AI incident notification channel.
Pilot AI-enabled penetration testing to harden critical infrastructure.
